## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: "entered into a double-blind peer review system and normally read by at least two assessors as well as by one of the Editors", and the editors' decision is final (guidelines, Wayback copy dated 2022-08-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20220802160239/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14684446/homepage/forauthors.html). The same page says papers should not be accessible via Google or similar searches, so they "should not appear in any form on websites". In the same copy, authors must also suggest at least three potential assessors with name, position, email and a sentence on why each is qualified; only one suggested assessor is approached at a time and use is at the editor's discretion |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Yes, within a network. The journal "participates in the Wiley Sociology and Social Welfare Publishing Network": at the editors' judgement, suitable papers not accepted may be recommended for referral to another journal in the network; the author decides, and previous reviewer reports go with the transfer (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02; the network's member journals were not read) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found on the pages read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No journal figure found. SciRev has 2 reviews and no round count (https://scirev.org/journal/british-journal-of-sociology/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source read |

## Format

> Source: the journal's guidelines, Wayback copy dated 2022-08-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20220802160239/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14684446/homepage/forauthors.html. This is the newest copy in the archive index, so any change since then is unverified. HTML comments in the page (script and layout notes) were excluded.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research manuscripts; research notes and commentaries; commissioned book reviews (5,000 to 6,000 words per the copy, peer reviewed). The LSE page adds a book-reviews section with occasional book symposia and review essays (https://www.lse.ac.uk/sociology/british-journal-of-sociology, read 2026-11-23). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-2026 are in Publication Frequency |
| **Word limit** | Research manuscripts "should normally be approximately 8,000 words", including notes and bibliography; "overly long papers will be returned without review at the Editors' discretion". Research notes and commentaries no longer than 2,500 words (copy dated 2022-08-02). The live LSE call for the "Scholarship as Struggle" project also sets commentaries at no more than 2,500 words (https://www.lse.ac.uk/sociology/british-journal-of-sociology, read 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The copy says "normally approximately", and says over-long papers can be returned without review; it states no exception procedure |
| **Abstract limit** | Up to 300 words; six keywords in order of importance (copy dated 2022-08-02) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 8,000 words. Harvard author-date system, bibliography after the notes; "op.cit., ibid." not to be used. The journal also says references may be submitted in any consistent style at first submission (free-format submission, same page) |
| **Supplementary material** | Supporting Information is allowed (additional tables, datasets, figures, multimedia), to be cited in the text and supplied in final format (copy dated 2022-08-02) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables on separate sheets with titles, minimal lines, electronic versions required; figure files in .eps at 800 dpi or .tif at 300 dpi, colour converted to greyscale (copy dated 2022-08-02; this reads as print-era wording and may be out of date) |
| **Style / submission format** | Free-format submission as a Word file; separate anonymised manuscript and title page; the title page carries data-availability, funding, conflict-of-interest, ethics-approval, patient-consent and permissions statements; ORCID asked; single quotation marks; "per cent" in text; "analyse" not "analyze"; double-line spacing (copy dated 2022-08-02) |

### Orientation

> Counts come from Crossref records of the journal dated 2021-01 to 2026-11-16: 615 journal-article records (this includes book reviews and issue-information items), of which 466 have an abstract (75.8%). A record counts when its title or abstract matches the regular expression listed in the AI-Research Notes (case-insensitive, word-bounded). Shares use the 466 records with abstracts as denominator; counts are lower bounds. Retrieved 2026-11-23, source https://api.crossref.org/journals/0007-1315/works.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Both. Method words: "survey" 72 (15.5%), "interview" 76 (16.3%), "panel/longitudinal" 31 (6.7%), "ethnograph-" 37 (7.9%), "historical/archival" 26 (5.6%); "theory" 102 (21.9%) and "conceptual" 20 (4.3%). "theory" also appears in empirical framing, so it does not identify purely theoretical papers. The editors say the journal "draws on an array of quantitative and qualitative methods" (https://www.lse.ac.uk/sociology/british-journal-of-sociology, read 2026-11-23) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Both present. Quantitative words: "survey" 15.5%, "regression" 3.4%, "causal" 3.0%, "quantitative" 0.6%, "experiment" 1.9%. Qualitative words: "interview" 16.3%, "ethnograph-" 7.9%, "qualitative" 6.2%, "participant observation/fieldwork" 4.1%. "mixed methods" 0.2%. A study can use neither word set, so the two shares cannot be added into a ratio |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Not scored from counts. The guidelines aim at papers "of the widest possible interest to a global general sociology audience" and original papers "covering the entire span of sociological thought and research" (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02). Topic words: "inequality" 99 (21.2%), "culture/cultural" 103 (22.1%), "states/politics" 175 (37.6%, broad regex), "organizations/firms/labor market" 65 (13.9%) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** The stated aim is "original papers covering the entire span of sociological thought and research" and "high quality, peer-reviewed articles of the widest possible interest to a global general sociology audience"; the editor "is particularly keen to publish work on current developments in research and analysis" (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20220802160239/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14684446/homepage/forauthors.html).
- **What kind of engagement?** The LSE page says the journal "features rigorous, original research that speaks to a general sociological audience" and has a tradition of work on "key social and political questions" (https://www.lse.ac.uk/sociology/british-journal-of-sociology, read 2026-11-23).
- **Article type and length**: manuscripts of about 8,000 words including notes and bibliography; research notes and commentaries up to 2,500 words; commissioned book reviews (https://web.archive.org/web/20220802160239/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14684446/homepage/forauthors.html, copy dated 2022-08-02).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: the "precarity of work and life" call asks how insecurity varies and invites "diverse methodological approaches" (qualitative or ethnographic, quantitative, mixed); the "New Sociology of Propaganda" call asks for abstracts of about 500 words to the guest editor by 2026-03-16, with full manuscripts due 2026-10-30 and standard peer review (https://www.lse.ac.uk/sociology/british-journal-of-sociology, read 2026-11-23).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection figure was found (SciRev: 2 reviews, https://scirev.org/journal/british-journal-of-sociology/). The guidelines say over-long papers "will be returned without review" and papers that appear to be early drafts will be returned and removed from assessment (copy dated 2022-08-02).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01 to 2026-11-16 whose title or abstract matches the regex listed in the AI-Research Notes; the denominator is the 466 records with an abstract (615 records in all; counts are lower bounds). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. The scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows were written for psychology and the humanities; where a row does not fit sociology it says so, and four rows were added.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 | "experiment" 9 (1.9%), "causal" 14 (3.0%); the word "experiment" includes survey and field experiments, e.g. a natural field experiment on headscarves (https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-4446.12811) |
| Quantitative survey / observational (added row) | 3 | "survey" 72 (15.5%), "panel/longitudinal" 31 (6.7%), "regression" 16 (3.4%), "administrative data/register/census" 11 (2.4%), "quantitative" 3 (0.6%). The LSE page says the journal draws on "an array of quantitative and qualitative methods" |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | "interview" 76 (16.3%), "qualitative" 29 (6.2%) |
| Ethnography and fieldwork (added row) | 3 | "ethnograph-" 37 (7.9%), "participant observation/fieldwork" 19 (4.1%) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph-" 0 of 466 abstracts. The row is a poor fit for this venue: no sociology-specific evidence was sought beyond the count |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | By the convention, "theory" 102 (21.9%) scores 3, but that overstates pure theory work because the word appears in empirical framing; "conceptual" alone 20 (4.3%) would score 2. Treat as 2-3. The journal also runs commentary pieces and a book-reviews section (LSE page) |
| Mixed methods | 1 | "mixed methods" 1 (0.2%); a special-issue call nonetheless invites mixed methodologies (LSE page, read 2026-11-23) |
| Comparative-historical / archival (added row) | 3 | "historical/archival" 26 (5.6%, includes papers that merely cover historical periods), "comparative-historical" 0 |
| Computational / text-as-data (added row) | 2 | "computational/text/ML" 5 (1.1%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | "meta-analysis" 0, "systematic review" 1 (0.2%). The row is a poor fit for this venue and is not evidence of rejection |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. In the 466 abstracts (abstract-only text; the counts do not cover titles or full text), 329 (70.6%) contain I, my, we or our (capitalised forms included); 232 contain "we" or "We"; 100 contain "I" or "my" (Crossref, regexes in notes; "our" can also be a generic plural, so this measures first-person wording, not necessarily a single author's voice). Examples seen in the first words of recent abstracts: "I argue that..." (https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-4446.12820), "We report the results of two natural field experiments" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-4446.12811), "we identify three processes" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-4446.12818); impersonal openings: "This article develops the concept of platformed atmospheres" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-4446.70188), "This article develops the concept of temporal structuration" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-4446.70185). The guidelines copy has no first-person rule |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling about 8,000 words including notes and bibliography; abstract up to 300 words (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02). No page-length statistics were taken |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Up to 300 words "giving a concise statement of the intention, results and conclusions"; six keywords in order of importance (same copy) |
| **Writing style notes** | Harvard author-date citations ("Connell 1987: 159-60" form), notes kept to a minimum and placed before the bibliography, single quotation marks, "per cent" in text and "%" only in notes, tables and figures, British spellings such as "analyse", and avoidance of sexist and racist language (same copy) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Among the 437 abstract-bearing Crossref records that list authors: 195 single-author (44.6%), 133 two authors, 62 three, 33 four, 7 five, 4 six, one each with 8, 14 and 70 authors; 29 abstract-bearing records list no author (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0007-1315/works, retrieved 2026-11-23). Book reviews, which carry no abstract, are not in this count |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The title page must carry an ethics-approval statement and a patient-consent statement (alongside data-availability, funding, conflict-of-interest and permissions statements); the journal follows Wiley's publication-ethics guidelines and is a COPE member (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20220802160239/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14684446/homepage/forauthors.html). The page does not say what happens if approval does not apply |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are common: 195 of 437 abstract-bearing Crossref records that list authors for 2021-2026 (44.6%; https://api.crossref.org/journals/0007-1315/works, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The title page asks for authors' affiliations and email addresses; no independent-scholar rule found (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02). Authors must name at least three potential assessors with positions, which may be harder without an institutional network (same copy; an inference, not a stated barrier) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The journal has adopted Wiley's "Expect" data-sharing policy: authors reporting original data are expected to archive it in a public repository where appropriate, must give a data availability statement, and are not required to share data to publish (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20220802160239/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14684446/homepage/forauthors.html) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind: authors anonymise the manuscript and supply a separate title page (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02). Preprint posting is allowed, yet the same page asks that submitted papers not appear on websites (see Preprint Policy) |
| **AI use** | See AI Policy: Wiley guidance requires disclosure of AI use at submission (copy dated 2026-05-18); no journal-specific text found |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no submission fee stated; APC unverified (OpenAlex lists 3840 dollars); see Open Access |
| **Authorship** | Authors must meet substantial-contribution, drafting and final-approval criteria and agree to be accountable; others go in the acknowledgments (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02) |

**Method note (Crossref):** `scripts/topic_trend_scan.py` is broken, so counts were taken from Crossref journal records (type journal-article, 2021-01 to 2026-11-16, 615 records, 466 with an abstract). A record counts when its title plus abstract matches the regex (Python `re`, IGNORECASE unless marked, HTML tags removed). Shares divide by 466. Many Crossref abstracts begin with the label "ABSTRACT", which matches none of the patterns. Author countries, OA status and work types came from OpenAlex single requests (one request each, no key, no 429); they cover all work types (641 works), whereas the Crossref counts cover the 615 journal-article records.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: manuscripts should normally be about 8,000 words including notes and bibliography, and "overly long papers will be returned without review" (Format; guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02). Research notes and commentaries are capped at 2,500 words.
- **Anonymisation**: double-blind review requires an anonymised manuscript and a separate title page (Peer Review; Practical Concerns).
- **Suggested assessors**: the 2022 copy makes it mandatory to suggest at least three potential assessors (Peer Review). The live page could not be read, so whether this still applies is unverified.
- **Prior or parallel publication**: articles must be original and not under consideration elsewhere (guidelines copy dated 2022-08-02; Peer Review).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; the guidelines copy is from 2022 and the live page could not be read.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher-reported first-decision figure is 17 days (home copy 2025-06-06) and 42 for 2022 (Review Cycle Time); submission to acceptance was 225 for 2022 (unit not printed). The editors aim at a 60-day average for papers sent out for review (LSE page). Figures differ by year and definition.
- **Selectivity**: the publisher-reported acceptance rate is 27% (home copy 2025-06-06) and 24% for 2022 (Metrics). The definition is not printed.
- **Reviewer nomination**: three suggested assessors with positions and a justification each (Peer Review; 2022 copy).
- **Preprint tension**: preprints are allowed, but the same page asks that the paper not be findable online (Preprint Policy), which a preprint would contradict.
- **Open access cost**: the OpenAlex-listed APC is 3840 dollars, unverified (Open Access).

### Best Suited For

- Sociological work with a general audience, drawing on qualitative or quantitative methods: the LSE page says so, and "interview" 16.3%, "survey" 15.5%, "ethnograph-" 7.9% of abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work on class, culture and stratification, or empire and postcolonial theory: "Cultural Capital and Social Class" is a top OpenAlex topic, "stratification/mobility" 10.7%, "Bourdieu" 6.0%, "decolonial/indigenous" 3.9%, and the most-cited recent items include anticolonial thought as social theory (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Work on race, gender and political sociology: "race/racism" 10.9%, "gender" 11.8%, "polarization/populism" 7.9% of abstracts and the DEI statement (Sensitive Topics).
- Authors responding to the open calls: the propaganda special issue (manuscripts due 2026-10-30, which has passed at the time of this entry), the precarity call and the commentary project (Special issues).
- Shorter commentary: up to 2,500 words (Format).

### Not Recommended For

- Authors needing a verified, current turnaround: the figures are from different years and the live page was not readable (Review Cycle Time).
- Papers far above 8,000 words (Format).
- Experimental or computational work as the main method: "experiment" 1.9%, "computational/text/ML" 1.1% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences). The counts show these are less frequent here, not that they are rejected.
- Work in autoethnography or systematic review: 0 and 1 of 466 abstracts (Methodological Preferences); absent, not rejected.
- Authors who need to post a preprint while keeping blind review intact: see Preprint Policy.
